chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Idris ibn al-Hasan, from Abu Ishaq al-Kindi, from Bashir al-Dahhan who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no goodness in one from our companions who does not acquire religious understanding. O Bashir! Verily, when the man from among them does not suffice himself with his jurisprudence, he becomes needful of them (others). And when he becomes needful of them, they lead him into the gate of their misguidance while he does not even realize it.'

key_terms.ضَلَالَة: Misguidance, straying from the correct path; the plural/possessive form here refers to the specific deviant paths of outsiders
key_terms.يَتَفَقَّهُ: To deeply study and understand Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh); implies not just surface knowledge but thorough grounding in religious law and understanding
key_terms.يَسْتَغْنِ: To be self-sufficient, to not be in need; here used in the sense of being independent in religious judgment through one's own knowledge

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the importance of religious jurisprudence for Shia followers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns his companion Bashir al-Dahhan — a perfume-seller of Kufa who had direct access to the Imam — about the spiritual and intellectual danger of religious ignorance among the Shia community. The Imam declares that a follower who lacks grounding in fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) inevitably becomes dependent on others, and those others — being of deviant orientations — will gradually lead him into misguidance without his awareness. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis that each believer must personally cultivate sufficient religious knowledge to remain spiritually independent and protected from deviation.
